title: William Vans Murray to James Madison, Paris, 26 June 1801 (No. 5, duplicate), coded postscript 'As to ... not a Word has yet been said', Founders Madison/02-01-02-0456

steps.what: Founders abstract 02-01-02-0456 and the 26 Murray->Madison 1801 letters: only the 7 May letter (18 May P.S.) is coded and decoded; letter dated Paris, not The Hague.
Found DD Netherlands vol. 4 on the NARA catalogue (naId 188770447, M42 reel 5) and downloaded all frames; the letter is frames 0397-0398.
Transcribed the coded P.S.: six groups 536 406 1004 264 1136 1075 (last group later corrected to 1175).
Read Wagner's decode of the 18 May 1801 P.S. (f.0372): 536 = the, 247 = Consuls, 1285.1181 = Gaudin, 712.621.1161 = Tribunate; 536 confirms the same code.
Looked for the original copy (sent via Le Havre) in DD France, M34 reel 9 (naId 188669701): it is the 1800 envoys' letter-book, no 1801 Murray despatch.
Scanned DD Netherlands vol. 3 (M42 reel 4) frames 0018-0211 with a subagent: Murray's 1797-98 coded despatches with a clerk's interlinear decode, about 150 pairs.
Matched the groups against the pairs: 1004 = -ed (intended, worked), 264 = neutral (neutral ministers), 1136 = -i- and 1175 = -ty (majority); proposed 406 = arm, 'the armed neutrality'.
Re-read the last group at 4x: 1175, not 1075. Checked 264.88 (f.0039R), 279.1136.1175 and 948.164.1004 (f.0167R) on the frames.
Searched vol. 3 frames 0212-0421 for group 406: decoded 406.1503s armies, 1086.406.1004 alarmed (f.0224R), 406.517 arming (f.0257L); 406.1004 armed (f.0365R). The prediction 406 = arm is confirmed.
P.S. As to the armed neutrality not a Word has yet been said (reading.txt, 6/6 tokens, all grade C).
Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 6 tokens, 6 types, en-modern order 4: reading -2.496 per letter; Verdict: too short.
Brice Dudout checked this project's reading of the coded postscript independently and agrees.

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The six code values were recovered from the contemporary interlinear decodes of Murray's other despatches in the same series (DD Netherlands vols. 3-4, M42 reels 4-5); 406 = arm was predicted from context and then found decoded three times.
outcome.notes: Key is partial: only the six groups of this letter (and the ~150 sibling pairs in scan notes, unverified) are rebuilt, not Murray's whole code. Catalogue correction: dated Paris, not The Hague; last group 1175.

credits.note: State Department clerks' and Jacob Wagner's interlinear decodes of Murray's 1797-1801 despatches (M42 reels 4-5)

texts.label: Postscript of No. 5, 26 June 1801
texts.summary: Murray, in Paris to exchange the ratifications of the Convention of 1800, tells Madison that in the conferences with the French ministers nothing has yet been said about the armed neutrality, the northern powers' league of 1800-01.

reading_review.note: One English sentence that reads as sense throughout; all six code values attested in contemporary decodes of the same code.

prior.where: Madison Papers abstract (PJM-SS 1:353, 1986): 'not deciphered (key not found)'; no decode on the duplicate; original copy not located.
